solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Style the rear in operation here, perhaps

definitions.text: Style the rear in operation here, perhaps

indicators.note: in operation suggests something being worked on and reshaped, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon remodels a patient's backside in a private clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of STYLE THE REAR, signalled by 'in operation'. The whole clue is also the definition: a famous London street of private doctors where such a bottom-lifting operation might be done.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Harley Street is lined with private clinics and surgeons, so a cosmetic operation could well take place there.

clue.text: Where choppers stack up, kept outside

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: kept means had, as in had or held onto

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a stack is a pile

explanation.surface: Helicopters wait in a holding pattern over a landing area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stack up' reads as aircraft circling while they wait to land, which is the misdirection; 'up' is the reversal signal in this down entry, and 'outside' does the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppers is slang for helicopters, and a landing pad for them is where they come down.

clue.text: Trails fugitives free from America

indicators.note: free from means the letter for America is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: fugitives are people who have run away

explanation.surface: Escaped convicts head off along paths, having got clear of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free from' removes A from RUNAWAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Runways are tracks or paths along which aircraft move, so they can be called trails in a loose sense.

clue.text: Cream for English tart that is not empty

parts.note: a moll is a gangster's girlfriend or a prostitute, as is a tart in slang
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: empty means the inside is removed, leaving just the outer letters of the word not

explanation.surface: Shoppers are offered an English tart with plenty of cream in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves NT from NOT. 'tart' and 'Cream' both suggest baking, but tart is a woman of easy virtue here.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a softening cream or ointment for the skin.

clue.text: Take off south on journey

parts.note: a journey is a trip

explanation.surface: An aircraft departs heading south on its journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off clothes, removing them from the body.

clue.text: Position of Queen, a piece capturing knight

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: capturing means the first group takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: the king is a chess piece
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess commentator describes the board as the queen's side takes a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts N inside A KING to give ANKING, after R for Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is one's place or standing in an ordered list, i.e. a position.

clue.text: Tire or tyre? (No, another part of car)

definitions.meaning: to tire is to wear out or drain someone completely
the pipe at the back of a vehicle that expels fumes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the word means tire or tyre, and is told neither: it is a different car component.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on tyre, a car part, and tire, its American spelling, then says the answer is a different car part with the sense of tire.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust someone is to wear them out, and the exhaust is the pipe system carrying a car's waste gases.

clue.text: Press forwards on park, taking on United

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first part sits above the second
taking on means the word takes in another piece

parts.note: forth means onwards or forwards, as in go forth
U is an abbreviation for United, as in football team names
an estate is a large park or grounds around a house

explanation.surface: A football reporter describes forwards on the pitch taking on Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking on' puts U inside FORTH to make FOURTH. 'Press' and 'forwards' suggest pushing ahead in football, but Press is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The press, meaning journalists collectively, is traditionally called the fourth estate of the realm.

clue.text: City of Gold, region found by Pizarro finally

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a land is a region or country

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the conquistador's name is used

explanation.surface: The Spanish conquistador Pizarro discovers a legendary golden city in the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes El Dorado, but the city is in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a city in Florida, home of major theme parks.

clue.text: Farms managed tailless game

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Someone ran a farming operation while playing some short-handed game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' removes the last S of CHESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranches are large farms, especially for raising cattle.

clue.text: Google's anger with Chinese vacillating

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads Google is

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering back and forth, so these letters are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: Google wavers in the face of anger from the Chinese authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Google's means is: Google is one of these. The surface recalls Google's real dealings with China.
explanation.definitionFit: Google is the best-known example of a web search tool, so it is defined by example.

clue.text: Painter's painter bound to flip about height

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so it reads painter is

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword abbreviation for an artist

indicators.note: about means the turned word is placed around the next letter
to flip means to turn over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to bound is to leap

explanation.surface: An artist's fellow artist is sure to do a somersault around something tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to flip' turns LEAP into PAEL, and 'about' puts it around H to give PHAEL. 'bound to' looks like 'certain to', but bound is the leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was a great Italian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Cheese plant?

definitions.meaning: a brand of soft processed cheese spread sold in tubes
a genus of flowering plants including primroses and cowslips

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the joke reading of a single cheese plant; it is a cheese and also a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Primula is a well-known brand of cheese spread and also the botanical name of the primrose family.

clue.text: Origins of Hell and damnation eternal, say

definitions.text: Origins of Hell and damnation eternal, say

indicators.note: origins means the starting points, so the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A preacher warns of hellfire and eternal damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five words after 'Origins of' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: a place of hell and eternal damnation, say.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth, used as another name for Hell, a place of eternal punishment.

clue.text: Greet with nice fizzy bubbly

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbles in motion, so the letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A host welcomes guests with a nice glass of sparkling champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne, which the surface suggests, but it is an adjective meaning lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubbly person is lively and full of vitality, which is what energetic means.

clue.text: Passionate former wife with guy possessing sex appeal

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: possessing means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable steadying a tent or mast
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An amorous former wife is with a man who has charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man but is a supporting rope.
explanation.definitionFit: An excitable person is easily roused, so passionate and quick to strong feeling.

clue.text: Biting sou'wester's beginning while in freezing cold

indicators.note: beginning means only the first letter of the hat's name is taken
in means the short word is placed inside the longer one

parts.note: arctic means extremely cold
as means while, as in as I was leaving

explanation.surface: A fisherman in a sou'wester is caught in bitingly cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou'wester is a waterproof hat. 'Biting' seems to describe the wind but means cutting in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarcastic remark is cutting and mocking, which is what a biting comment is.

clue.text: Dress is ripped without desire

indicators.note: without means outside, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: rent means torn or ripped
an aim is a goal or desire

explanation.surface: A dress is torn, without any wish behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for clothing, i.e. dress.

clue.text: One choosing to support a daughter?

definitions.text: One choosing to support a daughter?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: an opter is one who opts or chooses

explanation.surface: Someone elects to bring up and support a girl as their own child.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to support' places OPTER beneath A and D. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who adopts takes on a child by choice and brings them up as their own.

clue.text: Bird chasing the French label

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the bird comes after the next piece in the clue order

parts.note: the tit is a small bird
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A bird pursues a French person carrying a tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' here pictures the bird running along behind... yet written first, as if pursuing the French article down the line; read it simply as one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a name or label given to a book, film or person.

clue.text: Sack, right, by time waster

parts.note: to rifle is to ransack or sack

explanation.surface: Someone is sacked, rightly, for wasting time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismissing someone but means plunder; 'by' places T beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifler is someone who idles or fritters time away, a waster.

clue.text: Small getting six in Test

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: A minor score: a batsman gets a six in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, where a Test is an international match and a six is a big hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of small importance, minor.

clue.text: Fat girl stuck in a position …

indicators.note: stuck in means the name is lodged inside the other words

parts.note: a pose is a position held
Di is a short girl's name, for Diana

explanation.surface: An overweight girl is trapped in an awkward pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' signals the insertion; the surface is a cruel picture of someone stuck, but 'position' is a pose and 'girl' a short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means relating to fat, as in adipose tissue.

clue.text: Almost doesn't start in good time

indicators.note: doesn't start means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: Someone almost fails to begin on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops N from NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive early is to arrive in good time, before it is due.

clue.text: … sweating and tense before massage

indicators.note: before means this letter goes in front of the next piece

parts.note: T is a grammatical abbreviation for tense
oiling is rubbing oil in, as in a massage

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, someone is sweaty and tense before a rubdown.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 21-across for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Toiling means working hard, labouring so as to sweat.

clue.text: One puts up with English clergyman

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates an English vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts up with' looks like tolerating, but 'with' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is someone who builds or raises structures.

clue.text: Note, one relating to large amount

parts.note: a bill is a banknote
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about or relating to

explanation.surface: A banknote is linked to a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand million is a huge number, so it serves as a large amount.

clue.text: Bird's mostly pert, naughtily holding ends of robe

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so it reads Bird is

indicators.note: holding means the jumbled letters hold the next pair inside
naughtily suggests misbehaving, so the letters of the two words are jumbled
ends of means the first and last letters of the word robe

explanation.surface: A bird behaves cheekily, clutching at the edges of someone's gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' rearranges the ten letters of the two fodder words, and 'holding' wraps them round the pair from 'ends of' robe. 'mostly' looks like a trimming signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The storm petrel is a small seabird, also known under this longer name.
